title: dividerand
summary: Divide target indices randomly into training, validation, and test sets.

gpu_support.notes: dividerand produces host-side index partitions and uses RunMat's global random generator state.

description: `dividerand(Q,trainRatio,valRatio,testRatio)` randomly permutes the one-based target indices `1:Q` and divides them into training, validation, and test row vectors. `dividerand(Q)` uses the documented default ratios `0.7`, `0.15`, and `0.15`.
behaviors: `Q` must be a nonnegative integer scalar.
`Q` is capped at 10,000,000 so index partitions fail cleanly before excessive host allocation.
Ratios must be finite nonnegative scalar values, and at least one ratio must be positive.
Ratios are normalized before allocation, so they do not need to sum to one.
Returned indices are one-based row vectors and together form a random permutation of `1:Q`.
Empty partitions are returned as `1-by-0` numeric tensors.

faqs.question: Does dividerand respect rng?
faqs.answer: Yes. The random permutation is drawn from RunMat's global random generator, so `rng('default')` and numeric seeds make results reproducible.
